changes.before: Thus the three fields enter with equal weight; the denominator includes all accepted target-sector counts, not only those of the retained set.
changes.after: Thus the three fields enter with equal weight; the denominator includes all accepted target-sector counts, not only those of the retained set. All sixty retained final field-run records have \(N_s>0\): the records cover \(R=16,32\), seeds \(0,\ldots,9\), and fields \(s=0,1/2,1\). The separately supplied selected-record evidence exposes each final target-sector count vector, its field, size and seed, and its final accepted-shot count from \texttt{ada/adapt\_qsci/result.json}. It does not embed the full result file, trajectories or earlier iteration histories; those omissions remain explicit.

changes.before: Each field first retained at most \(R\) positive-count determinants, ordered by decreasing count and then increasing stored determinant index.
changes.after: Each field first retained at most \(R\) positive-count determinants, ordered by decreasing count and then increasing stored determinant index. The retained implementation asserts that at least one target-sector count is positive before selecting determinants. A zero-accepted-count iteration therefore aborts at that assertion, before pooling; the implementation supplies no resampling, uniform-weight or dropped-field fallback. The pooling formula describes the retained positive-count runs, not a prescription for an unobserved zero-count field.

changes.before: Original endpoint calculations select their spaces independently: their endpoint-energy difference and vacuum static subtraction do not come from a common projector.
changes.after: Original endpoint calculations select their spaces independently: their endpoint-energy difference and vacuum static subtraction do not come from a common projector. Specifically, let \(S_0\) and \(S_1\) be the independently selected vacuum and full-field spaces. The implementation takes \(E_0\) and its normalised ground-state vector from \(H_0|_{S_0}\), and \(E_1\) from the lowest eigenvalue of \(H_1|_{S_1}\). It extends the vacuum vector by zero to a vector \(u_0\) in the common 225-determinant parent basis. With \(V=H_1-H_0\) and the retained inactive-plus-nuclear endpoint increment \(\Delta c\), it evaluates \(D_{\mathrm{ind}}=u_0^{T}Vu_0+\Delta c\) and \(I_{\mathrm{ind}}=E_1-E_0+\Delta c-D_{\mathrm{ind}}\). Thus the static expectation uses the vacuum state in \(S_0\), whereas the full-field energy uses \(S_1\). The reported component errors subtract the exact-parent static and induction components and use the retained Hartree-to-kcal/mol conversion. This is the independently selected endpoint implementation, distinct from the common-space pooled calculation.
